title: Free resolution of localization on a slice
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, and let $f\in\mathcal O(U)$. On the slice site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], write $\mathcal O_U$ for the restricted ring sheaf and $\mathcal O_U[1/f]$ for the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the presheaf $(V\to U)\mapsto\mathcal O(V)[1/f|_V]$ of sectionwise localizations. Then the sequence of $\mathcal O_U$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]

$$
0\longrightarrow\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{d}\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal O_U\xrightarrow{q}\mathcal O_U[1/f]\longrightarrow0
$$

is exact, where $d((x_0,x_1,\ldots))=(x_0,x_1-fx_0,x_2-fx_1,\ldots)$ and $q((x_0,x_1,\ldots))=\sum_{n\geq0}x_n/f^n$ locally (on local representatives with finite support; these formulas extend by sheafification).

source.place: Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af), proof: the displayed free resolution of \mathcal O_f

proof.text: Work on the slice $\mathcal C/U$ of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], where $f$ restricts to a global section. Put $P(V/U)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal O(V)$ (finite-support sequences), and $L(V/U)=\mathcal O(V)[1/f|_V]$. Concretely, the latter consists of fractions $a/f^n$ with $(a,n)\sim(b,m)$ iff some $k\ge0$ satisfies $f^k(f^m a-f^n b)=0$; use the usual common-denominator addition and multiplication. Restriction applies the ring restriction to coefficients and to $f$, so preserves this relation. The displayed formulas give linear maps $D:P\to P$ and $Q:P\to L$, commuting with every restriction. In particular $D$ increases a finite support bound by at most one.

source.place: Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af), displayed free resolution in the proof, with the sectionwise verification expanded

proof.text: Fix $V/U$, write $R=\mathcal O(V)$ and $f=f|_V$. If $D(x)=0$, its zeroth coordinate says $x_0=0$; successively $x_i-fx_{i-1}=0$ implies $x_i=0$. Thus $D$ is injective on every object. Also $Q(Dx)=\sum_i x_i/f^i-\sum_i fx_i/f^{i+1}=0$, since the sums have finite support and $f$ is invertible in $R[1/f]$. Every fraction $a/f^n$ is $Q(a e_n)$, so $Q$ is surjective on every object.

source.place: Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af), displayed free resolution in the proof, with the sectionwise verification expanded

proof.text: Fix a section ring R and its element f. For n ≤ m, the vector a e_n - f^(m-n)a e_m belongs to im D, by induction on m starting with zero and adding D(f^(m-n)a e_m) at each successor step. Induction on a finite-support sequence, taking the maximum of the two indices in the additive step, gives x - a e_m ∈ im D for some m and a. If Qx=0, apply Q and use QD=0 to get a/f^m=0. Multiplying by the invertible image of f^m gives algebraMap(a)=0.

source.place: Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af), displayed free resolution in the proof, with the sectionwise verification expanded

proof.text: The localization equality algebraMap(a)=algebraMap(0) supplies k with f^k a=0, without cancelling f in R. The coordinate relation from the preceding step gives a e_m - f^k a e_(m+k) ∈ im D, hence a e_m ∈ im D. Adding this to x-a e_m ∈ im D proves x ∈ im D. The reverse inclusion is QD=0. This works with k=0, zero sequences, f=0, nilpotent f, and zero divisors. Sectionwise injectivity, exactness and surjectivity give short exact short complexes of modules. The evaluation functors jointly reflect the kernel limit; sectionwise surjectivity proves the presheaf Q is epi. Thus the presheaf sequence is short exact.

source.place: Tag 0997 (lemma-hom-from-Af), displayed free resolution in the proof, with the sectionwise verification expanded

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-sheafification-exact] to the ringed slice site and this exact presheaf sequence. It gives an exact sequence $0\to P^\#\xrightarrow{D^\#}P^\#\xrightarrow{Q^\#}L^\#\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules. This is exact module sheafification for a varying ring sheaf, not merely sheafification for constant coefficients.

source.place: Tag 03EI (lemma-sheafification-exact), applied on the slice site

proof.text: By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], maps $P^\#\to G$ to any $\mathcal O_U$-module sheaf $G$ correspond to presheaf maps $P\to G$. Such maps correspond exactly to families of module sheaf maps $\mathcal O_U\to G$: restrict to each coordinate, or sum their values on a finite-support sequence. These inverse assignments commute with restrictions. Thus $P^\#$ has the universal property of $\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\mathcal O_U$. By the definition in the item, $L^\#=\mathcal O_U[1/f]$. On the $n$th coordinate inclusion, $D(a e_n)=a e_n-fa e_{n+1}$ and $Q(a e_n)=a/f^n$. Their sheafifications therefore satisfy $D^\#\iota_n=\iota_n-f\iota_{n+1}$ and $Q^\#\iota_n(a)=a/f^n$ on sections from $\mathcal O_U$. The coproduct universal property makes these equalities determine the two maps uniquely; finite sums give exactly the displayed formulas on local finite-support representatives. This proves the entire displayed sequence, without assuming that a sheaf coproduct has sectionwise finite-support sections globally.
